api_lessons: Vec4D (and other API objects) must be constructed with `new` (new Vec4D(...)); calling Vec4D(...) without new crashed Cheetah3D.

title: Adding a Plane
summary: Q&A on how to create a plane from a script: script-type entry points, doc.addObject, and a polygon script building a plane with UVs.

api_lessons: Entry points by script type: Macro main(doc); Tool buildUI(tool); Polygon object buildUI(obj) once when added plus buildObject(obj) on every update.
doc.addObject(PLANE) creates a parametric plane; doc.addObject(POLYGONOBJ) creates an empty polygon object whose core() can be filled.
core.addPolygon(n, false, [Vec3D...]) adds a polygon directly from positions; alternatively core.addVertex(false, Vec3D) returns indices for core.addIndexPolygon(n, indices).
UVs: core.setUVCoord(polyIndex, cornerIndex, new Vec4D(u1, v1, u2, v2)) — Vec4D packs UV set 1 and UV set 2.
obj.addParameterSelector(name, [options], ...) returns the selected index; parseInt() the value from getParameter before switching on it.
notes: The original poster reported the help file's constant spelling ('Plain') was not recognized; tg_jp's code uses PLANE.

summary: Request for a Node-style require(); Martin declines, and users post an eval-based library loader that reads .js files from a Scripts/Library folder.

api_lessons: There is no require()/import in Cheetah3D's JavaScriptCore engine; share code by reading a library file with File and eval-ing it.
Use indirect eval (var geval = eval; geval(src)) so library definitions land in global scope; direct eval inside a function did not work on 7.0.18 per the author.
obj.scriptPath() gives the running script's path; derive the user's home with a regex to locate ~/Library/Application Support/Cheetah3D/Scripts/Library/.
File I/O: var f = new File(path); f.open(READ_MODE); var s = f.read(f.size()); f.close();
Library files are re-read at run time, so they can be edited without restarting Cheetah3D.
Native plug-ins / loading external unsigned code is not supported due to Mac App Store sandbox rules (Martin, 2012).
notes: aaronparr's variant (post 94069) has a syntax slip ('main(caller)' missing 'function'). Martin states JavaScript is the chosen scripting language and recommends Unity integration for games.

title: buildUI() function
summary: Q&A on why adding parameters crashed Cheetah3D: buildUI-only parameter functions and required arguments.

evidence.author: aaronparr
evidence.quote: I don't believe you can call buildUI() from main(). I crashed when calling this code from main

evidence.author: aaronparr
evidence.quote: if you avoid using any of the arguments in this case it causes a crash. I was ignoring the booleans

api_lessons: addParameter* functions (addParameterString/Float/...) must be given ALL documented arguments, including the trailing booleans; omitting optional-looking args crashes Cheetah3D rather than throwing.
The docs say addParameter* calls are only valid inside buildUI(); calling buildUI() manually from a Macro's main() still crashed (with the missing-args bug confounding).

Macros cannot easily attach custom editable properties to arbitrary scene objects; parameters added in a Tool's buildUI go on the tool pane, and there was no documented way to set which script a dynamically created script tag runs.
notes: Context: Neverwinter Nights MDL importer wanting custom per-object properties. Archived snippet is the crashing (incomplete-args) version.
